record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: Are nanoscale clustered or phase-separated states a generic feature of correlated oxides and related materials beyond manganites, including cuprates and Eu-based semiconductors, and in Eu compounds is the correct description ferromagnetic polarons or instead a nanocluster-based phase-separation picture?

evidence.quote: Are the nanoclusters found in manganites and cuprates (see below) characteristic of other oxides as well? ... They suggest that many compounds are intrinsically inhomogeneous. ... Are Eu-based semiconductors truly described by ferromagnetic polarons as believed until recently, or is a nanocluster picture more appropriate?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider strongly correlated electron systems whose low-energy phenomenology is shaped by competing magnetic, charge, and orbital orders, including:

(a) doped transition-metal oxides such as the high-temperature superconducting cuprates and other complex oxides;
(b) Eu-based magnetic semiconductors and semimetals (for example, low-carrier-density europium chalcogenides and hexaborides), in which mobile carriers couple strongly to the localized Eu 4f spins.

Two competing microscopic descriptions of the inhomogeneous electronic state near a magnetic transition in such materials are:

(i) Ferromagnetic (magnetic) polarons: isolated mobile carriers, each self-trapped by polarizing a small ferromagnetic cloud of localized spins around it, embedded in a paramagnetic background.

(ii) Nanocluster-based phase separation: an intrinsic coexistence of nanometer-scale regions of two (or more) distinct electronic/magnetic phases (e.g., ferromagnetic metallic and antiferromagnetic/paramagnetic insulating) arising from electronic phase separation, rather than from independent single-carrier polarons.

Address the following:

1. Determine whether the existence of nanoscale phase-separated or clustered electronic states is a generic feature of strongly correlated oxides and related compounds beyond the manganites, in particular establishing whether such inhomogeneity occurs intrinsically in the cuprates and in Eu-based magnetic semiconductors.

2. For Eu-based magnetic semiconductors, decide which of the two descriptions (i) or (ii) above gives the correct microscopic account of the inhomogeneous state near the magnetic ordering temperature, or characterize precisely a regime in which a crossover or coexistence between the two pictures applies.
artifact.category_tag: Strongly correlated electron systems and phase separation
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent experimental and theoretical work has produced strong evidence that nanoscale electronic inhomogeneity is widespread beyond manganites, in cuprates and in Eu-based compounds such as EuB6, Eu5In2Sb6, and EuCd2P2. In EuB6, fluctuation spectroscopy, nonlinear transport, and imaging studies support magnetic-polaron formation that percolates into a phase-separated state, suggesting the two pictures (ferromagnetic polarons vs. nanocluster phase separation) are reconciled as different regimes of the same percolative scenario rather than mutually exclusive. A fully general microscopic theory establishing universality across all correlated oxides remains incomplete.

status_evidence.snippet: Fluctuation spectroscopy and weak nonlinear transport reveal magnetically driven electronic phase separation consistent with percolation of magnetic polarons.
status_evidence.claim: Evidence in EuB6 supports a unified polaron-percolation/phase-separation picture.
